items.name: PanVA
items.subtitle: Variant Analysis within Pangenomes
items.abstract: PanVA is a visual analytics system for exploring genetic variant data within pangenomes. It enables genomics researchers to compare sequence variation across multiple reference genomes simultaneously through coordinated, interactive views. The project was developed in collaboration with 9 biotechnology companies and plant breeders in the Netherlands and Belgium, all associated with the Virtual Laboratory for Plant Breeding.

items.name: Multipla
items.subtitle: Multiscale Pangenomic Locus Analysis
items.abstract:
Multipla supports multiscale exploration of pangenomic loci, revealing structural variation and sequence context at different levels of detail. The project was in collaboration with visualization experts from Sweden as well as bioinformaticians specialized in rose and pepper genetics.

Related to this project on structural variation, we also looked at redesigning sequence tube maps to support overview and detail views with aggregations.

items.name: Visualization Authoring
items.subtitle: Personas & Blended Interfaces
items.abstract:
This project investigates how genomics researchers author interactive visualizations. Through interviews and probes with 30 domain experts we identified key user personas and authoring tasks and techniques, from which we distilled key design considerations.

A parallel project explored how different authoring techniques can be combined in one interface, to support the creation of expressive and learnable authoring tools.

items.name: Agentic Authoring
items.subtitle: Interactive Multiscale Visualizations
items.abstract: Exploring how LLM-powered agents can assist domain experts in authoring interactive genomics visualizations, reducing the technical barrier while preserving expressive control over multiscale data visualizations. We explored vanilla LLM capabilities versus different agentic setups to understand the strengths and limitations of several architectural schemes in supporting visualization authoring.

items.name: Sycamore
items.subtitle: Synthetic Personas
items.abstract: Recruiting many domain experts for user studies is important, but also very resource intensive. In this project we explored the potential of synthetic user personas — not to replace, but to complement human user studies — using LLM-generated personas grounded in real user persona data.

Grateful to receive a travel grant for BioVis @ ISMB 2026.
